caption: Stump Pairs Across Areas
content: Paired stumps do not necessarily need to be placed within the same Area.

content.caption: Example
content: Let's think about how to re-solve these Areas so as to @g{rule/complete_forest/flower}{make flowers bloom on all roads}.

To do so, at least one stump pair is required somewhere. However, there is no way to complete either the left or right Area while also creating a stump pair for each. This is because both Areas are too small: stump pairs are difficult to create in the first place, and even if one is created, @g{tips/complete_block/stump/parity}{the color imbalance of 2 caused by that stump pair} cannot be compensated for.

In cases like this, instead of considering the two Areas separately, you should consider creating a stump pair that spans across Areas. Doing so means that each Area's color imbalance is off by only 1, making the mismatch easier to compensate for.
In fact, by placing the tiles as follows, you can complete the Areas while making flowers bloom on all roads.
